title: competitive-probing-program-enterprise-rag-slo-behavior-matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Run a small-batch, repeatable probing program that maps how candidate third-party models behave under real enterprise RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) workloads and our SLO constraints. Deliver a behavior matrix that surfaces consistent failure modes, latency and cost characteristics, and procurement trigger signals (e.g., unacceptable hallucination rates, cold-start latency, context truncation failure) to inform fallback strategies and vendor negotiations.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Experiment design doc with sampling plan for 6 representative enterprise workloads (search+summarize, contract-question-answering, chat-assist with tools, multi-turn RAG, embeddings lookup + generation, chunked-long-context RAG).
2) Implementation harness (not a full product integration) that runs parallel probes against 4 candidate models/variants across three simulated infra regions and two hardware profiles. Harness will collect per-request: end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), tokenized cost, hallucination/error labels (binary + confidence), semantic-similarity drift vs. ground truth, token-generation anomalies (truncation, early EOS), and KV-cache miss patterns.
3) Behavior matrix artifact (spreadsheet + interactive dashboard snapshot) that tags models with trigger flags: LATENCY_EXCEEDS_SLO, HALLUCINATION_HIGH, DEGRADES_AFTER_MINUTES, INCOMPATIBLE_TOOL_CALLS, EMBEDDING_DIVERGENCE.
4) Procurement-trigger playbook: concrete thresholds and suggested negotiation levers (SLA credits, pinned variants, dedicated reservations) mapped to each trigger.
5) Exec one-pager summarizing risk & opportunities for Redwood Dedicated and Private offerings.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change production routing or billing. It is scoped to experimentation and recommendations for PM/Eng leadership decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment design doc reviewed and approved by ENG + Research (comments resolved)
Harness runs 10k synthetic+20k replayed enterprise queries across candidate models and produces raw logs in S3/GCS
Behavior matrix populated with automated flags for the five trigger categories and validated on two ground-truth datasets
Procurement-trigger playbook reviewed with Revenue/Legal and assigned clear negotiation thresholds
One-pager and dashboard snapshot presented in the weekly GTM sync
